newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF non-bank study group to review CP, bond limits.
newsitem.headline: MOF non-bank study group to review CP, bond limits.

text.p: A study group under Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is to look at lifting limits on commercial paper and corporate bond issues by non-bank financial institutions, a ministry official said on Tuesday.
The group, which met for the first time on Tuesday, will reach a decision by March 1997, the official said.

A government panel promoting deregulation has called for Japan to lift limits on the use of funds raised by non-banks through commercial paper (CP) and corporate bonds by the end of fiscal 1996/97. It said any steps recommended by the group should be carried out starting from April 1997.
Currently, non-banks are not allowed to use funds raised through the issue of commercial paper for making loans. Funds raised through corporate bond issues are to be used only for acquiring assets.

The group, to meet once or twice a month, will also consider disclosure of bad loans held by the non-banks. The group will ask people from the financial industry to give their views in the next meeting, to be held in late November.
Non-bank financial institutions make loans but, unlike banks, do not take deposits, funding their lending activity instead by borrowing from banks.
